nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis, annealing, and acid wash of Ru-based multimetallic oxides
nodes.procedure: Synthesis of Ru-based multimetallic oxide samples (up to four metal elements) via: (1) hydrothermal precursor mixing at 25-60°C for 6-24h, (2) annealing/pyrolysis at 400°C or 500°C for 6h alternating in 1:1 ratio per batch, (3) acid wash post-treatment to remove impurities and perovskites like CaRuO3/SrRuO3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sample C consists of small, single-crystalline RuO2 particles ~5 to 10 nm in diameter, interconnected to form a polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) results of the 12 samples are provided in Fig. 5 (A and B) and figs. S26 to S28. In general, the samples obtained consist of small, single-crystalline RuO2 particles, ~5 to 10 nm in diameter, interconnected to form a polycrystalline structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sample C's lattice spacing of the (110) lattice plane expanded to 3.25 Å compared to standard 3.12 Å (RuO2-400-Pre) and 3.09 Å (RuO2-400).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As indicated by Fig. 5C and fig. S26A, sample C's lattice spacing of the (110) lattice plane expanded to 3.25Å when compared to the standard lattice spacing of the pure Ru samples both before (RuO2-400-Pre, 3.12Å) and after (RuO2-400, 3.09Å) the acid wash process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy-dispersive x-ray analysis via TEM shows second to fourth metal elements uniformly distributed with non-aggregated signals in sample C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Subsequent energy-dispersive x-ray analysis via TEM in Fig. 5D further strengthened our belief that the second to fourth metal elements are uniformly distributed with non-aggregated signals detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: Sample C dominated by RuO2 phase after acid wash with impurities removed; no traces of CaRuO3 and SrRuO3; noticeable leftward shifts in XRD peaks indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Having been acid washed, sample C seemed to be dominated by the RuO2 phase (Fig. 5E) with the impurities in C-Pre well removed, and no traces of CaRuO3 and SrRuO3 could be found like that in A/B/D.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Mn-2p spectra shows Mn²⁺ 3/2 peak shift to lower binding energy post-acid wash indicating Mn doping into RuO₂ lattice; Ru 3d 3/2 peak shifts higher vs RuO₂; Ru>4+ species ratio 35.24% (highest among A-D).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mn²⁺ 3/2 peak of sample C shifts toward a lower binding energy... Ru 3d 3/2 peak of sample C exhibited a slight shift toward a higher binding energy compared with RuO₂... sample C has the highest ratio (35.24%) among A to D.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms show BET surface areas: sample B 94.35 m²/g, A 88.88 m²/g, D 74.47 m²/g, C 39.92 m²/g, RuO2-500 45.58 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We also conducted nitrogen adsorption-desorption isotherms of A to D (fig. S22). The fitting results indicate a consistent trend: sample B exhibits the highest Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 94.35 m² g⁻¹, greater than that of A at 88.88 m² g⁻¹, D at 74.47 m² g⁻¹, and C at 39.92 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) measured for ECSA calculation: sample B largest at 2357 cm², C 923.3 cm², RuO₂-500 ultralow at 310 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further evaluation of the samples' electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) is presented in fig. S21, where the ECSA values were calculated on the basis of the measured double-layer capacitance (Cdl). B exhibits the largest ECSA (2357 cm²), and C has the lowest ECSA among the four (923.3 cm²).
